profile.summary: GraphDTA predicts how strongly a drug molecule binds a target protein. The drug is given as a molecular graph rather than a string, and the protein as its amino acid sequence; the output is a single affinity value. The point of the method is the drug side: the authors argue that a graph is a more natural representation of a molecule than a SMILES string, and they encode it with a graph neural network while a one dimensional convolution reads the protein sequence.
profile.summary_source_locator: Europe PMC record: abstractText, Summary; models/ginconv.py: GINConvNet

summary_quotes.text: We propose a new model called GraphDTA that represents drugs as graphs and uses graph neural networks to predict drug-target affinity.
However, these models represent the drugs as strings, which is not a natural way to represent molecules.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The drug is turned into a graph of atoms with 78 features per node, and one of four graph networks encodes it: GINConvNet, GATNet, GAT_GCN or GCNNet. In GINConvNet, five GIN convolution layers of width 32 with batch normalisation are followed by sum pooling and a linear layer to a 128 wide drug vector. The protein sequence is mapped character by character to integers, cut or padded to 1000 positions, embedded with width 128, and passed through a single one dimensional convolution with 32 filters and a kernel of 8, then a linear layer to a 128 wide protein vector. The two vectors are concatenated and sent through dense layers of 1024 and 256 units to one output unit, trained with mean squared error.

sections.title: Data and training settings
sections.body: The repository ships the Davis and KIBA datasets, which the README says were downloaded from the DeepDTA repository, with the fold files that define the split. For Davis the preparation script converts the affinities to a log scale. Training runs for 1000 epochs with a batch size of 512 and Adam at a learning rate of 0.0005. Two scripts differ in how the best model is chosen: training.py keeps the model with the best mean squared error on the test data, following DeepDTA's practice, while training_validation.py holds out 20 per cent of the training data and selects on that instead.

quotes.text: In this section, a model is trained on 80% of training data and chosen if it gains the best MSE for validation data, which is 20% of training data.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The four drug encoders are the versions that matter: a result must say which of GINConvNet, GATNet, GAT_GCN and GCNNet was used, on which dataset, and with which of the two training scripts, because the selection rule differs between them. The code was read here at commit 6162245c6776684b391d30610850fe7077478435. The paper's availability statement says pre-trained models are at the repository; the file listing at this commit contains no model file, and the sources read do not explain the difference. A separate Zenodo deposit, doi 10.5281/zenodo.3603523, is given for the scripts and data behind the paper's statistical analysis.

quotes.text: The proposed models are implemented in Python. Related data, pre-trained models and source code are publicly available at https://github.com/thinng/GraphDTA.

strengths.text: It is a small, plain baseline that many later papers reuse: four interchangeable drug encoders, two datasets shipped with their folds, and a training run driven by three command line numbers.
strengths.source_locator: README.md: Train a prediction model; git tree listing: models, data

strengths.text: No protein structure is needed. The protein side is the amino acid sequence only, and the drug side is built from canonical SMILES.
strengths.source_locator: create_data.py: seq_cat; git tree listing: proteins.txt, ligands_can.txt

strengths.text: The authors report that the graph representation of drugs beat both non deep learning models and competing deep learning methods on their task. This is their claim in the paper abstract.

quotes.text: We show that graph neural networks not only predict drug-target affinity better than non-deep learning models, but also outperform competing deep learning methods.

strengths.text: Both model selection rules are provided, one following DeepDTA's practice of selecting on the test set and one with a proper validation split, which makes the comparison with earlier work explicit.
strengths.source_locator: README.md: Train a prediction model, Train a prediction model with validation; git tree listing: training_validation.py

quotes.text: The model is chosen if it gains the best MSE for testing data.
This follows how a model was chosen in https://github.com/hkmztrk/DeepDTA.

limitations.text: Protein sequences are cut at 1000 characters, so anything beyond that position is discarded.
No trained weights were found in the repository at this commit, although the paper says pre-trained models are available there, so in practice a user trains the model themselves.

run_guide.summary: Build the Davis and KIBA data in PyTorch format, then train one of the four GraphDTA variants and get its test metrics.
prerequisites: conda, with the environment the README describes: python 3, rdkit from conda-forge, pytorch with torchvision and cudatoolkit, and pytorch_geometric with its torch-scatter, torch-sparse, torch-cluster and torch-spline-conv wheels.
A CUDA GPU. The training script selects a cuda device by index, and the README notes the device name may need changing in the code.
No separate data download: the Davis and KIBA files are in the repository.
No licence is declared for the code or the shipped data.

steps.title: Install the libraries
steps.shell:
conda create -n geometric python=3
conda activate geometric
conda install -y -c conda-forge rdkit
conda install pytorch torchvision cudatoolkit -c pytorch
pip install torch-scatter==latest+cu101 -f https://pytorch-geometric.com/whl/torch-1.4.0.html
pip install torch-sparse==latest+cu101 -f https://pytorch-geometric.com/whl/torch-1.4.0.html
pip install torch-cluster==latest+cu101 -f https://pytorch-geometric.com/whl/torch-1.4.0.html
pip install torch-spline-conv==latest+cu101 -f https://pytorch-geometric.com/whl/torch-1.4.0.html
pip install torch-geometric

notes: The record comes from the Marijan and Tanasijevic 2026 benchmark preprint, which is on bioRxiv only (pdf at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.08.31.748056v1.full.pdf) and was not fetched in this pass, so nothing here is taken from it; Europe PMC shows no PMC copy. Discrepancy for a human: the paper's availability statement says pre-trained models are at the repository, but the GitHub file listing at commit 6162245c holds no model file, and nothing read explains the difference. The context_length of 1000 in the structured rows is the max_seq_len in create_data.py, a preprocessing cut on the protein sequence, not a learned context window. Three sibling records in this batch (PGraphDTA, PLM-GraphDTA, DeepGraphDTA) are variants of this model; their facts were not copied from here.
